claims.explanation: Desoxycortone is a mineralocorticoid receptor (NR3C2) agonist, and its selective antiproliferative pattern is best explained by NR3C2 expression: lines with high mineralocorticoid receptor signaling (e.g., renal, lung, colorectal, and melanoma lines) are sensitized, while lines with low NR3C2 or high glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1) tone are protected. Co-occurring alterations in PI3K/AKT pathway genes (PIK3CA, PTEN, MTOR, STK11) and ARID1A/SMARCA4 chromatin-remodeling genes further modulate response, consistent with steroid receptor crosstalk with growth-factor and chromatin pathways.

features.basis: mineralocorticoid receptor is the annotated target of desoxycortone; high expression predicts agonist response
glucocorticoid receptor signaling antagonizes mineralocorticoid-driven growth inhibition
PI3K pathway activation is enriched in least-affected lines (T47D, MDAMB361, HT115, RT112, HGC27, MKN1)
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, enriched in protected lines (DMS273 is exception but pathway logic)
STK11 loss is enriched in least-affected lines (22RV1, SNU840, MDAMB175VII, LU99)
ARID1A mutations appear in many least-affected lines (22RV1, T47D, MDAMB361, MDAMB175VII, SW1088, VMCUB1)
SMARCA4 mutations appear in several most-killed lines (EKVX, COV434, NCIH1703)
TP53 mutations are near-universal in most-killed lines but also common in protected lines, so weak alone
BRAF mutations appear in several most-killed lines (IGR37, CAL12T, NMCG1, G361)
KRAS mutations appear in several most-killed lines (LOVO, NCIH1792, ASPC1)
CTNNB1 mutations appear in most-killed lines (KE39, LOVO, LXF289 is exception)
CDKN2A loss appears in many most-killed lines (BHY, CAL12T, RD, NCIH1703, ASPC1)
